title: 2023-10-10 historical archive and reuse of prior index
summary: A previous read-only local run of the fully extracted ADSB.lol daily archive reported 53,575 per-aircraft gzip JSON traces in 256 directories and 48 heatmap gzip tiles; 23 aircraft within 120 km of a public Paphos reference across the union UTC windows, with 17,815 retained full-day points. These are an external handoff, not independently reproduced in the current cloud workspace.
invariants: The 07:00–11:00 UTC primary window yielded 12 aircraft and 94 nearby points; 10:00–14:00 UTC fallback yielded 13 aircraft and 96 nearby points.
Nearest reported point was about 65 km from the public Paphos reference; no point was within 50 km. Sparse ADS-B points are not an absence-of-aircraft proof.
Existing local outputs: paphos_aircraft.sqlite, candidate_summary.csv, source inventories, README in the 2026-11-05 Codex index run output folder.
Do not propagate private apartment receiver coordinates, filenames from source recordings, or aircraft lists from private file inventories into public repository artifacts.
Coordinate systems must be explicit: WGS84 lon/lat, altitude datum, relative frame and UTC time basis. No invented trajectory interpolation over evidence gaps.
procedure: Inspect the existing indexed output in place if accessible; establish source hashes and record counts.
Query using indexed UTC and spatial cells; fetch exact source trace samples only for ranked candidate aircraft.
Record PTS authority and instrument clock correction separately from ADS-B UTC.
Keep source coverage, airspace observer coverage and sampled proximity distinct.
